fullPassage: In a business environment devised to provide as many goods and services to customers as possible, efficiency the ability to produce results using the least amount of time was traditionally the metric by which achievement was gauged. But efficiency may not be the best measure of success. In the modern economy, where churning out products has led to automation and other shortcuts, effectiveness the ability to achieve the desired outcomes that best fulfill company goals should also be considered. In a manufacturing company, a machine that assembles twice as many products as a human worker might seem efficient. If this machine requires two attendants to operate and maintain it, however, it has an overall negative effect on the company. The company is producing more products, but the cost of each product has risen; despite requiring the same human capital, there is the additional cost of the machine and its maintenance, rendering its effectiveness lower. In short, simply increasing output does not always translate into improved performance or profitability. Thus, businesses should seek a balance between efficiency and effectiveness so that they can utilize resources optimally while maximizing profit.
